items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: The Sam Wooding-Rae Harrison Jazz Band poured on the jazz... His vivacious partner and wife, Rae Harrison performed the spiritual and blues songs.

ctx.x: But do you remember what kind of songs they were singing? Were they singing sweet songs? The girls?

Well, they sang all kinds of songs. There was a song they called 'Shimme-Sha-Wobble'. And there was a song called, "I Wish I could Shimmy Like My Sister Kate". And then there was songs called, "I Lost You, So Why Should I Care". And then, we had the others, you know, different types of songs, and that's one thing Old Man Brown told me, too, he said -- and I never forgot it. Later on, I told a little lady working with me, Rae Harrison, I told her the same thing. He said, "Sam, don't set up on that piano and play…

audience and see what condition they're in. Now, if you see a lot of people sitting around there like they're moonstruck or something like that, what are you going to play the "Strutters' Ball" for, what are you going to play like that? You want to go into something like, "I Lost You, So Why Should I Care", or something like that." You know what I mean?
